# Native SDR final output color (LRTimelapse 7.5.5)

`lrt-color-plan-7.5.5.json` records 162 direct invocations of the installed
7.5.5 build 1059 render color and metadata helpers: six source labels, three
gamut values, three dynamic range values and three video range values.
The observations include unsupported HDR/wide gamut combinations. Only the
ordinary BT.709 SDR output branch is implemented here. This was a helper
measurement, not an end-to-end application render. No license state was changed.

The observed command scales RGB to full-range `yuv444p10le` with Lanczos,
sets BT.709 metadata, then uses zscale for full/limited range and final
subsampling. Input and output swscale flags are
`print_info+accurate_rnd+bitexact+full_chroma_int`. The initial swscale RGB
conversion uses its default matrix; setting BT.709 metadata afterwards does
not make that conversion equivalent to a direct RGB-to-BT.709 zscale pass.
The implementation retains this behavior rather than substituting a matrix.

`lrt-sdr-output-color-8.0.1.json` records 144 SHA-256 hashes and byte counts
from the installed bundled FFmpeg 8.0.1 (Gyan essentials): two dimensions
(64x32 and 32x16), native/scalar CPU paths, full/limited ranges, three output
formats (420 8-bit, 422 10-bit, 444 10-bit), and six deterministic synthetic
RGB16 patterns. `Filter` is the independently constructed measurement graph.
Test patterns are generated by `nativeColorSource` in the test file. No source
images, binaries or proprietary code are redistributed.

`TestNativeOutputColorGoldenPlanes` runs the production filter builder against
these full-plane hashes. It is opt-in because the reference pins the bundled
FFmpeg version. Other builds may round differently.

```powershell
$env:LRTL_COLOR_FFMPEG='C:\Program Files\LRTimelapse 7\ffmpeg.exe'
go test ./internal/lrtl -run '^TestNativeOutputColor' -count=1 -v
```

The regular suite includes 24 backend argument cases (two profiles, four
codecs, three ranges), preset defaults/overrides, invalid input preserving
existing files, and unchanged still export/preview. When FFmpeg is available,
12 real video cases cover PNG/TIFF, H.264/H.265/ProRes HQ and both ranges.
Three opaque 64x32 RGB16 frames are decoded independently by Go and FFmpeg;
the Go video output is compared with a separately encoded reference command
following the observed native graph. All decoded YUV bytes must match.
With ffprobe, dimensions, fps, frame count, format and color metadata must
also match. Codec loss is included in both branches; CRF 0 is not assumed
to guarantee identical decoded samples across all codecs/builds.

These initial comparisons cover final encoding only. The subsequent
[native spatial path](lrt-native-spatial-color-7.5.5.md) adds pure Go initial
RGB16-to-YUV10 conversion and YUV-domain unsharp/CAS for even output sizes
without overlays or fade, with 84 additional real video comparisons. The
[native temporal path](lrt-native-temporal-color-7.5.5.md) adds deflicker,
denoise and airplane removal under its listed conditions, with 72 scalar
reference video comparisons. Other combinations retain the RGB approximation.
JPEG decoding now has [separate measured coverage](lrt-jpeg-input-8.0.1.md),
including progressive/restart inputs and native working planes. The original
comparisons in this note do not establish ICC, nonidentity geometry, HDR/wide gamut or complete native
application video parity.
